title: Thali Builder
description: A round thali plate with a staple grain in the center and six katori (bowls) for dal, vegetable, main dish, side, sweet and spices. Learners switch among seven regions (Punjab, Bengal, Kerala, Gujarat, Sindh, Sri Lanka, Nepal), click each bowl to read about the dish, and read how grain, climate, geography, faith and trade shape each region's food. A checkbox swaps the main dish between common vegetarian and non-vegetarian examples.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Food and foodways
Regional cuisines
Geography of food
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Compare the everyday thalis of seven South Asian regions slot by slot.
Explain how staple grains, rainfall, coasts and mountains shape regional cuisines.
Identify ingredients that reached South Asia through the Columbian Exchange.
Explain how faith and food rules affect whether a regional plate is usually vegetarian.
prerequisites: Knowing where the rivers, deltas, coasts and mountains of South Asia are (Chapter 1)
Knowing that different faiths in South Asia have different food rules (Chapter 5)
keyQuestions: Why is rice the staple in Bengal, Kerala and Sri Lanka, while bread is the staple in Punjab?
Which regions in the sim cross modern national borders?
Which ingredients on these plates came from the Americas?
Why is a Gujarati thali usually vegetarian, while a Bengali thali often includes fish?
misconceptions: Curry is one dish eaten everywhere in South Asia.
All South Asian food is very spicy.
Chili peppers are native to South Asia.
Naan is the everyday bread of every South Asian family.
controls: Click or tap the center or any katori on the plate
